answer: A grove of agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to be vouched for through a growing vine of real work: every new agent must first complete small, verifiable tasks attested by established peers, and its reputation accrues slowly like rings on a tree. A falcon-style watchdog that samples random attestations and slashes stake when it finds fake clusters makes mass-producing identities unprofitable, because each fake must pay the full cost of earned trust before it can extract value.
